terra.problem: The text does not say nobody asked Simon, that he had not volunteered, or that he never saw this coming.
“The soldiers had the route covered” adds an unsupported detail about their route.
The text does not say Simon had never planned to carry the cross.
The text says the wine was offered, but does not mention a cup being held out.
The closing observations are generic and add little to the explanation: “a sad little scene” and “worth reading twice.”
Mark 15:26 says the charge was inscribed against Jesus, not that it was written over Him. That detail needs an outside reference.
The claim that the title appears elsewhere in the Gospels needs a reference.
Mark does tell us more than what the passersby shouted: he also says they shook their heads and heaped abuse on Jesus.
Mark does not identify Golgotha as a hill. The line also stretches the account by suggesting everyone there was against Jesus.
The identification of Elijah as a prophet needs an outside reference.
The identifications of Moses as Israel's leader and Elijah as a prophet need outside references.
The identifications of Abraham as Israel's forefather and Elijah as a prophet need outside references.
The claim that a robe being torn appears in other stories needs an outside reference.
Mark records what the centurion said, but does not explicitly say that he never mocked Jesus.
Mark does not say how long the women had been with Jesus or identify Golgotha as a hill.
